facts.fact: launchd parses -s as single-user and passes sflag to jobmgr_init.
PID1 selects the System root session. jobmgr_init_session constructs /bin/launchctl bootstrap -S <session_type> and appends -s when sflag is true.
bootstrap_cmd parses -s and invokes system_specific_bootstrap(sflag) for the System session.
system_specific_bootstrap disables mdns/ds search modules and invokes do_single_user_mode(sflag) before the later loopback/sysctl/rc/LaunchDaemons startup sequence.

do_single_user_mode loops while do_single_user_mode2 returns false. That function forks; parent calls waitpid(child,&wstatus,0) synchronously, while child attaches the console and execl(_PATH_BSHELL,"-sh",NULL). Normal parent execution cannot pass this wait while the child shell remains alive.

Loopback setup, sysctl.conf/rc work and LaunchDaemons loading follow the single-user wait. Successful single-user shell exit allows this later bootstrap to proceed. launchctl is therefore not generally inert or safe to allow by name alone.

Optional startup-debugging fatal-signal handlers can enter crash-debug mode; they are not a normal background network-management loop. A crash or changed process context must remain failure, not accepted normal ancestry.

known_wrapper_source.finding: Finite shell wrapper invokes darwin-net-egress in the foreground in an if command; no background operator/job. The client must finish before status/uname/return commands run. Reading this script is source evidence only.

Permit exact string launchctl only when encountered as a non-self ancestor on that verified chain and its parent is exactlyPID1. No unrelated launchctl, wrong-parent launchctl, second launchctl, or prefix/name-near-match is allowed.
Retain audited foreground shell/script roles for the remaining ancestors; do not replace ancestor checks with a process-name allowlist.

Bind the new candidate to the single-user boot and fixed foreground wrapper/source/artifact provenance. Keep the single-user shell alive and retain the established sealed-input/no-other-guest-network-actor execution contract.
Treat shell exit, process inventory change, signals/crashes, unknown rows or uncertain ancestry as failure. A one-time inventory is evidence of context, not a kernel network-ownership lease.
